item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is the more mergeable patch because it implements the requested convenience API with the established multipart helper while avoiding A's explicitly forbidden, SDK-wide retry/body-buffering change. Both patches incorrectly duplicate FilesService.Add instead of routing Upload through it, but B's defect is localized and straightforward to fix.","reasons":["B adds the exact Upload signature, validates inputs before any request, uses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", and preserves FilesOption query/request-option handling.","A changes RawClient.Do to buffer nearly every nonstandard io.Reader across the entire SDK, directly conflicting with the contract to preserve Add behavior and avoid unrelated retry refactoring.","A's global buffering changes memory usage, source-reader error timing, and streaming semantics for Add, Update, and unrelated endpoints; its WithNoRetry exception introduces further behavior outside the requested scope.","Both candidates copy Add's request construction and response decoding instead of calling s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), violating the required reuse pattern and creating duplicate machinery that can drift from Add."],"risks_a":["Broad RawClient behavior change violates frozen scope and can unexpectedly buffer very large request bodies throughout the SDK.","FilesService.Upload duplicates Add rather than routing through it.","Changelog and README document newly invented global buffering semantics that the maintainer contract explicitly excludes."],"risks_b":["FilesService.Upload duplicates Add's internals rather than delegating to Add.","Tests omit empty-filename/nil-content validation and source-reader failure coverage required by the contract.","The retry test does not set RetryAllMethods and does not read or compare the multipart body on each attempt, so it weakly verifies streamed-content replayability."]}
